primary_meaning: Divine judgment or the outpouring of God's wrath upon the wicked (often depicted as treading/trampling grapes that yield blood)

alternatives.meaning: Christ's redemptive suffering and the outpouring of his blood (the 'mystic winepress' motif in which Christ himself is pressed)
basis: Medieval and early-modern Christian iconography and devotion

alternatives.meaning: Material abundance, blessing, and agricultural prosperity (overflowing winepresses as a sign of covenant favor)
basis: Deuteronomy 15:14 and similar OT prosperity texts

alternatives.meaning: Element of the vineyard parable representing Israel or the kingdom (the prepared facilities of the vineyard)

notes: In prophetic and especially apocalyptic Christian interpretation the winepress is overwhelmingly a stock image of eschatological wrath; the abundance and Christological readings are well-attested but secondary or context-specific.
